newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras may go for "exotic" bond.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras may go for "exotic" bond.

text.p: Brazilian state oil company Petrobras may choose an "exotic currency" such as Italian lira as the denomination of bonds it intends to issue by the end of 1996, private Invest News agency said.

According to Orlando Galvao, Petrobras' financial director, the choice of currency for the issue, which should total $125 million, will depend merely on the cost and the speed with which the bond can be set up.
Galvao added that Chase Manhattan bank, which managed Petrobras issues earlier this year, would not take part in the next launch.
Petrobras has already issued bonds worth $375 million this year. The funds are to be used in production and exploration of oil and purchasing of equipment.
Next year, the company aims to try to raise a further $600 million, Invest News said.
Petrobras will also start negotiating its next ADR issue, the second this year, in the next 20 days, Galvao said.
Petrobras officials were not immediately available to comment on the report.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
